summary: IdP logout redirect fragment (#) stripped by ingress rewrite causing tenant session rehydration failures in private VPC
description: Issue summary: After configuring OIDC single-logout (RP-initiated) for MindMesh's private VPC deployment, logout redirect responses that include URL fragments (e.g. '#session_state=...&id_token_hint=...') are having the fragment portion stripped by an ingress rewrite. Impact: end users are intermittently left in a partially signed-out state; console and admin API calls that rely on session rehydration fail with 401/403 and users cannot complete tenant-bound operations. Environment: private deployment in VPC (customer-managed NGINX ingress in front of Redwood identity-proxy) in us-east-1. First observed: 2026-02-28 during SSO integration testing following customer IdP update.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer configures OIDC RP-initiated logout with a logout redirect containing a fragment (e.g. https://console.customer.example/logout#session_state=abc&id_token_hint=ey...)
2) IdP issues redirect to Redwood's ingress endpoint which rewrites upstream URL to identity-proxy service, but internal rewrite removes fragment component
3) identity-proxy receives request without fragment, cannot locate session_state/id_token_hint, attempts session rehydration fails
4) Console responds with 401 or shows stale "signed in" UI; subsequent API calls requiring tenant context return 403 until user signs in again
expected_behavior: Logout redirect preserving fragment (or alternative transport e.g., query/state) so identity-proxy can complete RP-initiated logout/session cleanup and rehydrate tenant session appropriately.
actual_behavior: Fragment portion of redirect (everything after '#') is not visible to identity-proxy due to rewrite and proxy trim; logout flow fails, leaving inconsistent session state and 401/403 on tenant operations.
logs: 2026-02-28T18:03:12Z identity-proxy received GET /logout (no fragment, no session_state param) headers: Authorization: <redacted>, Cookie: rw_session=...
2026-02-28T18:03:12Z identity-proxy WARN session_rehydrate: no session_state found, falling back to cookie; tenant lookup failed => 401
Console client UX trace: SSO logout redirect returned 302 to /logout but application did not complete RP logout: session cookie still present
investigation_notes: Initial triage with customer shows IdP is correctly issuing redirect with fragment. Packet capture at customer edge confirms fragment present in Location header of browser-level redirect. However, fragments are client-side only and should not be sent to the server; root cause appears to be a relying-on-fragment pattern in customer's IdP configuration (using fragment to carry state instead of query/state param) combined with our ingress rewrite rules and identity-proxy assumptions. We reproduced by configuring a test IdP that issues logout redirects with fragments and saw same behavior behind NGINX rewrite. Additional finding: some older browsers will expose fragment if a 302 uses absolute-URI and subsequent client-side code reads and posts it; customer's SPA expects fragment processing client-side but our console relies on server-side rehydration for RP logout when behind private deployment. Cross-team sync: discussed with edge/ingress team and identity-proxy owners. See packet capture and nginx rewrite logs attached in comment.
root_cause: Combination of customer IdP using URL fragments to deliver logout/session_state and server-side rewrite/proxy design that does not receive URL fragments (fragments are not part of HTTP requests). Additionally, the private console integration expected server-driven rehydration for RP logout, which doesn't work when state is carried in the fragment. The ingress rewrite did not compensate for this client-side only transport.
workaround: 1) Short-term: ask customer to change IdP logout binding to include session_state and id_token_hint as query parameters or to use 'state' param (recommended). 2) Customer can enable a lightweight client-side handler in their console SPA that extracts fragment and POSTs to /internal/sso/logout with body carrying session_state for server to consume (we provided example script).
resolution: Planned: update support docs to call out 'Do not use URL fragments for RP-initiated logout state; use query/state parameters'. Engineering follow-up: add a guidance check in private deployment quickstart and a diagnostic in identity-proxy that logs heuristics when it detects logout without state but with suspicious user-agent/browser referrer. Longer term: add optional client-side helper snippets in the private package to capture fragments and forward them to identity-proxy endpoints.
resolution_notes: On 2026-03-03 we provided customer with a short-term config change and sample client-side handler. Customer validated fix in staging and reported successful logout flows. Engineering ticket INT-9112 opened to add diagnostic logs and quickstart docs update; PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7890 creates a 'fragment-diagnostics' warning in identity-proxy and docs changes. Follow-up: add public KB article and include a test for fragment-derived logout in the private deployment E2E suite.
